5.4.0.title: Landscape & TV
highlights: The Android app now works in landscape, with two columns on wide screens.
You can use it with a TV remote or game controller. The selected button lights up.
The app is now set up for Android TV and Meta Quest. Android TV is tested; Quest is not yet tested on a real headset.
The app finally has the ARMGDDN skull icon instead of the default Android robot, including the round style and the themed style on Android 13 and newer.

5.3.1.title: A Steadier Finish
highlights: Fixed a rare crash that could happen when a download finished just as the Companion window was closing.

5.3.0.title: Share My Setup
highlights: After Check my setup, a new button copies a short report you can paste in the ARMGDDN chat so Tulip can help from real facts.
The report leaves out your name, folder names and anything private. It holds the check results and recent warnings from the app's log.

5.2.0.title: Check My Setup
highlights: A new button in Settings, Check my setup, looks at the things behind most install and launch problems before you download.
It checks free space on your download drive and your Windows temp drive, your download folder's location, your antivirus, and the redistributables games need.
Each line says what is fine and what to fix. If redistributables are missing, it points you to /redists in the ARMGDDN chat.

5.1.0.title: A Clearer Low-Space Warning
highlights: If your download folder is on another drive, the low-space box now says so: your download folder is fine.
It explains that setup always unpacks its temporary files into the Windows temp folder (C: by default), wherever you save or install the game.
It links to a new Wiki guide for moving your temp folder to another drive.

5.0.26.title: Tidier Linux Installs
highlights: The Linux install command now saves the app to ~/Applications instead of your Downloads folder, and running it again updates the same file.
Website downloads now work when the app is in a folder with a space in its name. Before, the link between the website and the app silently did nothing.
The leftover .old backup after an in-app update is now cleaned up automatically.
Thanks to Dirk for the suggestion.

5.0.25.title: A Clear Message If You Left The Group
highlights: If your account is no longer in the ARMGDDN group, downloads can't start. The app now says so and tells you how to fix it, instead of showing "session expired".
To fix it: rejoin the group, complete the CAPTCHA Rose sends you within an hour, then retry the download.
The website shows the same message as soon as you click Download.

5.0.24.title: Clearer Download Errors
highlights: When a download stopped without a clear reason, the app could show a meaningless startup message as the cause. It now shows the normal "Download failed" message with an error code instead.
If you need to report a failed download, include that code and the game name so we can find the cause faster.
Messages for expired links, full disks and dropped connections are unchanged.

5.0.23.title: Auto-Extract Finds a Way
highlights: Auto-extract now works on Linux systems where the app's built-in unpacking tool refuses to start. If it can't run, the app tries a private copy of it, and then the 7-Zip already installed on your system.
If no unpacking tool can start, the app now says so plainly and tells you to install 7-Zip from your package manager, instead of "Failed to validate archive contents."
The app's log now records exactly why an extraction fails, so problems are quicker to track down.
Thanks to Dirk for the detailed testing.

5.0.22.title: Auto-Extract Works on Linux
highlights: Fixed auto-extract on some Linux and Mac installs. On 5.0.21, extraction could still fail with "Failed to validate archive contents" even though the tool was bundled, because the system wouldn't let the app run it from where it was installed. The app now falls back to running its own copy from its data folder.
Windows is unchanged. Extraction already worked there.

5.0.21.title: Auto-Extract Fixed
highlights: Fixed auto-extract. If you were on 5.0.18, 5.0.19 or 5.0.20, extracting your downloads inside the app failed with "Failed to validate archive contents before extraction." A packaging mistake on our side left out the tool the app uses to unpack archives. It's back, and this update puts it in place again.
If the unpacking tool is ever missing, the app now says so plainly and asks you to report it, instead of showing a confusing validation error.
Thanks to seb for reporting it.

5.0.20.title: Newer Engine, Clearer Drive Errors
highlights: Updated the app's built-in browser engine to its newest major version, with the latest security fixes from Chromium. Everything works the same.
Mac users: this version needs macOS 13 or newer. Macs on macOS 12 simply won't be offered the update and can keep using their current version.

If the drive you picked for downloads isn't connected (an unplugged external drive, say), the app now tells you which drive is missing and to reconnect it or choose another download folder, instead of a generic "can't create the folder" error.

5.0.19.title: Android App Update
highlights: The Android app has been rebuilt on the latest Android app framework, with security updates throughout. Login, layout and downloads were tested on a real phone.
Nothing changes in the desktop app. This update is for Android users.

5.0.18.title: Safer and Clearer
highlights: Updated the app's built-in browser engine to its latest security release, picking up 11 rounds of Chromium security fixes.
If your antivirus quarantines the download engine, the app now tells you how to restore it and exclude the app's folder, instead of just saying it failed to start.
Checking for updates no longer shows a confusing error when GitHub is busy. The app just asks you to try again in a little while.

5.0.17.title: Quieter Behind the Scenes
highlights: Cleaned up how the app reports problems back to us. Everyday hiccups, like an expired download link, a rate limit, or your connection dropping, no longer count as bugs, so the real ones stand out and get fixed faster.
Nothing changes in how downloads work. This update is just housekeeping.

5.0.16.title: Fewer Failed Downloads
highlights: If a download fails because your internet dropped, the app now waits for your connection to come back and resumes it automatically. No more coming back to a failed download that just needed a Retry.

Before a download starts, the app now checks the drive your Windows temp folder is on (usually C:). The game's setup unpacks its temp files there even when you install elsewhere. If there isn't enough room, it warns you up front instead of after the download finishes.

If your PC's date/time is wrong, or your antivirus is scanning secure connections, downloads can't connect. The app now tells you exactly that and how to fix it, instead of failing with a vague error.
Cancelling or pausing a download no longer shows a "Download failed" message.
Fixed a crash when opening the app while it was closing.

5.0.15.title: Smoother Installs
highlights: Auto-extract now unpacks games straight into the download folder, like 7-Zip's "Extract here", instead of into an extra subfolder. That extra folder could make file paths too long for Windows, and setup would then "finish" instantly with nothing installed.
If your C: drive doesn't have enough free space for a game's installer, the app now tells you when the download finishes. Setup unpacks to C: first even when you install the game somewhere else.

5.0.14.title: Riding Out Connection Drops
highlights: If your internet drops for a moment during a download, the app now waits for it to come back (up to 5 minutes) and carries on, instead of failing right away.
Fixed large multi-part games failing on their later parts with "Download link expired". Each part now gets its own fresh links when it needs them.

5.0.13.title: Recovering From Dropped Connections
highlights: If your connection to a mirror drops partway through a file, the app now switches to another mirror and carries on, instead of failing the download.
Error reports now include the recovery steps the app tried, so we can fix stuck downloads faster.

5.0.12.title: Honest Speed Limits
highlights: Max Concurrent Downloads now goes up to 6, the most the server allows per user. If you had it set higher, it's been set to 6 for you. You won't lose any speed, because the extra slots were never being used.
Fixed a misleading "Server load is high" warning that showed up even when the server wasn't busy, for anyone with the setting above 6.

5.0.11.title: Smarter Mirror Switching
highlights: If a mirror is rate-limiting a file or has hit its download limit, the app now switches to another mirror automatically instead of failing.
Fixed downloads that could fail with "Download link expired" when the real problem was one busy mirror. The app now tries a different mirror before giving up.

5.0.10.title: Fits Every Screen
highlights: Fixed Settings being cut off at the top and bottom on ultra-wide and short screens. It now scrolls, so every option is reachable.
Behind the scenes: crash reports now include a little more detail about graphics issues, so they're easier to fix.

5.0.9.title: Clean Exits
highlights: Fixed a crash that could happen when closing the app while a download was still running.

5.0.8.title: No More Graphics Crashes
highlights: Fixed the app closing itself on some PCs because of a graphics driver problem. If your graphics card can't keep up, the app now switches to a safe drawing mode and keeps running.
You won't notice any difference in how the app looks or works in the safe mode.

5.0.7.title: Better Bug Hunting
highlights: The app now sends an automatic error report when something goes wrong, like a crash or a download that fails, so problems get spotted and fixed without you having to report them.
Reports are stripped of personal info before they're sent: no download links or tokens, no IP address, and your user folder name is hidden.
Prefer not to send them? Turn off "Send error reports" in Settings.

5.0.6.title: Back on Its Feet
highlights: Fixed downloads that could freeze partway through a file and sit there forever. If a connection dies mid-download, the app now notices within about a minute instead of never.
Stalled files now retry automatically with a fresh link, up to 3 times, before giving up. No more restarting a download by hand just because your connection hiccuped.
If a file still can't be resumed after those retries, the error now says so clearly instead of the misleading "stalled at 0 B/s".

5.0.5.title: Unstuck
highlights: Found and fixed a real bug where downloads could quietly stop making progress partway through, especially after a retry or a pause — the app would still say it was downloading, but nothing was actually happening.
Added better internal diagnostics so if a download ever does stall again, we'll be able to see exactly why instead of guessing.

5.0.4.title: Fixed a Download That Wouldn't Stay Finished
highlights: Fixed a bug where a download recovering from an expired link could get wrongly marked as failed while it was actually still finishing — the app would then look like it "restarted" a completed download. Thanks to Kaizo for reporting this one with logs, which made it possible to track down.
Downloads should now recover cleanly from expired links and mirror switches without any UI weirdness.

5.0.2.title: Space, Mirrors, Priority
highlights: Free space is now shown in Settings and while downloads are running — you'll get a warning if space gets tight mid-download instead of finding out the hard way.
Mirror auto-switching now catches a few more failure types, and you'll actually see it happen ("Switched mirrors ×2") instead of it being invisible.
Drag a queued download to the top of the list to have it start first.
This popup! You'll see what changed right after every update from now on.

5.0.0.title: A Fresh Coat of Neon
highlights: The whole app got a visual revamp — same neon look, cleaner everywhere.
Status badges are now color-coded so you can tell downloading/completed/failed/paused apart at a glance.
Settings panel got restyled toggle switches and a proper dropdown.
Toast notifications for things like "Settings saved" and "History cleared".
